title.narrative: Civil Rights Defenders Ethiopia, Phase II 2023-2026
Civil Rights Defenders Etiopien, Fas II 2023-2026

description.narrative: Insatsens övergripande mål är att skapa förutsättningar för människorättsarbete genom att öka säkerheten och den organisatoriska kapaciteten hos människorättsförsvarare, intensifiera arbetet för unga och kvinnliga människorättsförsvarare, rehabilitering av civilsamhället i konfliktdrabbade områden, och stärkt kapacitet att övervaka kränkningar av mänskliga rättigheter.

The overall objective (s) of the contribution is creating enabling environment for human rights work through increasing safety and organisational capacity of human rights defenders (HRDs), intensifying the work of young and women human rights defenders, rehabilitation of civil society in conflict-affected areas, and strengthened capacity to monitor violations of human rights.

Outcome 1: A vibrant civic space with resilient, capable, and impactful human rights organizations and human rights defenders Outcome 2: Human rights organizations engage in efforts to bring accountability for human rights violations. Outcome 3: HRDs have safety and security to conduct impactful human rights work. Outcome 4: Human rights organizations and HRDs will be able to influence core agenda of the national dialogue process.

The below is based on Annual Report for 2024 (UM2023/05992/ADDI-66)
Outcome 1: Resilient and Effective Human Rights Organizations and HRDs Significant efforts have been made to strengthen the capacity of human rights organizations (HROs) and defenders (HRDs). Five organizations improved governance structures and strategic planning, while two developed internal systems and policies on anti-corruption and gender equality. Internship programs enabled 15 young women to gain professional experience and contribute to legal aid for detainees. In conflict-affected areas, five HROs in Tigray were rehabilitated with support for staff, equipment, and strategic documents. Psychosocial assistance was provided to ten HRDs in Afar, Amhara, and Tigray. A comprehensive conflict impact analysis resulted in a roadmap with six strategic recovery actions. Collaboration was strengthened through a joint shadow report to the UN UPR, two networking events with 50 CSOs, and initiatives promoting disability rights. Impact: Civil society has increased resilience, capacity, and cooperation.
Outcome 2: Accountability for Human Rights Violations Capacity building included training 24 HRDs (mostly women) in Monitoring, Documentation, and Reporting (MDR) and investigative techniques. Four MDR grants enabled documentation of violations: CJ monitored childrens rights in prisons and published a report. DFA built MDR systems in Benishangul Gumuz and trained 30 HRDs. Gurmuu developed MDR guidelines and produced monthly reports. EHRCo focused on internally displaced persons rights. DtE pursued two precedent-setting environmental cases and trained 15 lawyers in strategic litigation. Impact: Local actors strengthened their ability to document and pursue accountability for rights violations.
Outcome 3: Security and Safety for HRDs Digital security was prioritized through training nine HRDs as trainers. Seven conducted follow-up sessions reaching 75 HRDs and journalists, focusing on password management, two-factor authentication, and documenting tech-related gender-based violence. Physical and psychosocial security programs were delayed due to regulatory and safety constraints. Impact: HRDs improved digital security, though gaps remain in physical and psychosocial protection.
Outcome 4: Influence on National Dialogue Despite political delays, HROs established mechanisms to monitor and influence the national dialogue. CEHRO developed a monitoring matrix and regional committees, submitting four human rights agendas to the commission. CARD published two reports on transparency and launched a petition with 3,000 signatures, prompting dialogue with the commission. Impact: Foundations for continued influence on the dialogue process have been established.
Overall Conclusion: The project achieved substantial progress despite a shrinking civic space and security challenges. Through capacity building, rehabilitation, networking, and strategic actions, HROs and HRDs have gained resilience, resources, and influence.
